# The Broken Nose Goblins

*Pages PDF 30-41*

## The Broken • Nose Goblins
## **Takers of Many Dwarf Holds**
Goblin tribes are usually subservient to tough Orc Warbosses. They prefer to skulk around and let the brutal, bolder greenskins do most of the fighting. The Broken Nose tribe are different, because they’ve shown they can pack a punch far greater than most Goblins. This is not because they are especially brave or fearsome — it’s down to their success in deploying pilfered war engines. 

In other ways, the Broken Nose tribe are typical of Goblins that dwell on the plains, mountains, and hills of the Old World. They’re a little more disciplined and organised than most tribes, for as long as they keep trouncing their enemies, they rally around Boggrub Legbiter’s banner. 

The tribe are recognisable from the battered noses which give them their name. Each of them has been through an initiation ceremony, where the warchief ceremonially punches them in the face and breaks their nose. 

For the rest of their lives, they wear their crooked or snub nose as a sign of allegiance and subservience to Boggrub. 

In 2470 IC, the tribe came to prominence in the eastern World’s Edge Mountains. The Broken Nose raided Karak Azul and surrounding Dwarf outposts and defeated several armies. A number of captured war machines were amongst the spoils, including the trebuchet they dubbed ‘Skull Crusher’ and the organ gun ‘Lead Belcher’. 

The ensuing rampage erupted into a full Waaagh! under Boggrub, as they tore through Dwarf and Human resistance on a march of destruction to the west. Over the years, the Broken Nose strayed further through the Black Mountains, attacking settlements in Averland and the northern Black Fire Pass. Today, they are chiefly active in the Appucini Mountains and Vaults, near Karak Bhufdar and the Dwarf outpost of Zarakzil. Boggrub is eager to stay on the move and once again he’s eyeing up the Empire and its plentiful supply of war machines. 

## **Disposition of the Broken Nose**
The Broken Nose tribe is made up of 160–200 Goblins and a fluctuating mass of hangers-on. 

- Boggrub’s Mob are the toughest Goblins. They get the biggest share of the spoils after a fight and are marginally less likely to try to usurp the warchief. 

- Amongst them is Gutbug, the tribe’s second-incommand, assigned to the war machines. 

- The Shaman Rutbagger is a weathered Goblin with leathery skin and filthy robes made from a looted Dwarf banner. 

- The other 24 Goblins in Boggrub’s Mob have the Elite profile. 

Boggrub’s champions are Stink, Ratbrain, and Pusboil (Elite template). These are thoroughly disreputable characters who lead their own mobs of reprobate Goblins. Numbers in these mobs vary considerably and they often break into smaller groups as needed. For total numbers, add 2d10 to any of the following. 

- Stink’s Dogjabbers — 45 spear-wielding Goblins with the Soldier template, led by Stink. 

- Ratbrain’s Stickas — 48 Goblin Skirmishers with short bows. 

- Pusboil’s Guard — 40 Goblin Soldiers armed with spears, shields, and ideas above their station. 

The war machines are the Broken Nose’s pride and joy. They include the ‘Skull Crusher’, a looted Dwarf trebuchet with rune magic to improve accuracy, and the ‘Lead Belcher’, another of the tribe’s acquisitions from the Dwarfs. This is an organ gun combined with a howitzer… technology the Goblins don’t understand but truly appreciate for the devastation it causes. Sometimes the tribe has other war machines, including spear chukkas and wolf-drawn chariots (known to the Broken Nose Goblins as “Boneshakers”). 

## **Hangers-On**
Broken Nose conquests attract bands of greenskins looking to benefit from the tribe’s victories. They stick around as long as the going is good. 

- Toerag’s Ankle Slashers are a gaggle of Snotlings. The Goblins tolerate them because you can always eat a Snotling when food is short. At any given time, there are 5d10 Snotlings with the tribe. Titchy Toerag is a Snotling Elite. 

- From time to time, ‘Wolfy’ Datzda (Elite) and his 21 wolf riders join the Broken Nose. These are wolfmounted Soldiers with spears and shields. 

- Badbreath is a nasty Stone Troll followed by a band of six more Stone Trolls (see page 88). They’re useful when the tribe is in a fight and a nuisance when they’re not. 

## **Uniform**
The Broken Nose raided a Tilean textile merchant’s caravan several years ago, now many of them wear grubby jerkins made from black and mustard-coloured cloth. 

## **Battlecry**
“Ooar-ya? Ooar-ya?” 

## Black (Market) Powder
The Lead Belcher eats up black powder, which causes problems for Gutbug. Getting a reliable supply is tricky, as he can’t rely on ambushing travellers to obtain enough. Boggrub wants to trade with an unscrupulous Tilean merchant and Luciano Maranza of Trantio seems a likely option. Now they need to make him an offer… 

## Bloody Cousins
The Shaman Ratscrote Boggobbler was thrown out of the Broken Nose for being too bloodthirsty. He went off to form the Bloodied Nose tribe, who now dwell east of Black Fire Pass. Under Ratscrote’s leadership, they started worshipping a minor god or Daemon called Khakkekk, alongside Mork and Gork. Khakkekk demands blood sacrifices and continual violence. The Broken Nose hate the Bloodied Nose and would be very happy to see them wiped out. 

## Olde Weirde’s Incunabulum
If Sigmar wielded every hammer that had been ascribed to him, wore every amulet, and blessed every relic, he would have barely had time for anything else. Nevertheless, Pfaff would not be put off and sniffily gave us the ultimatum that if we did not accompany him, he would set off in pursuit of the creatures alone. What could we do? 

Should Taal, Sigmar, and all the gods conspire to create a creature of piteous cowardice and wretched misery, then they might be hard-pressed to conceive of something much better than the common Goblin. As rats infest the sewers, so does the Goblin infest the scrub and the forest. These green-skinned creatures snivel and skulk in the margins of the Empire, harassing her people and raiding her towns. Their trickery and opportunism derive from their cowardice. They snatch babies from their cots and eat them. They ambush and kill lone travellers. They band together and burn whole villages, leaving no survivors behind them. 

The priest had discovered one Goblin laggard hiding in the crypt. Sovrissniz was tormenting the poor thing. Kaia told her she was wasting her time. The Elf had already had a look around and discovered the warband’s tracks clearly enough, in the muddy ground. We would easily be able to follow them and did not need to subject the creature to such pain. Sovrissniz grumbled theatrically. ‘It’s your lucky day, Grobi,’ she said, giving the creature an almost friendly cuff on the side of the head. 

All citizens of the Empire are familiar with stories of Goblins, the Goblin and the shoemaker, the Goblin who got stuck up the chimney, the Goblin and the duck. These are staple tales for children, and through them everyone knows what Goblins are like. Am I correct? Well, perhaps. But the truth of things is a little more complex and interesting than Johann Farmer and his wife would have you believe. I have encountered Goblins several times on my travels and have sometimes found them to be more than the mindless creatures of destruction and spite that they are painted. 

I stepped in to rescue the Greenskin, before Sovrissniz could be even more friendly and I am not saying that the creature looked at me as a Human might look at a friend in gratitude, more perhaps as a dog might look at a master. But there was certainly an appreciation in its eyes that I had spared it further pain. 

We tied it to a tree so that it would not give us away and followed Kaia further into the hills. I trust that I am not spoiling the tension of the account to reveal that I did indeed survive the episode, but it is worth noting that when we returned that way, the Goblin was gone and the only sign of its presence was the rope we had tied it with, lying on the ground, untied. 

We were in southern Averland. Professor von Gronighof was on the trail of an exotic sword from Khemri, which will be the subject of a forthcoming monograph. But we were distracted by a temple to Sigmar that had been all but razed to the ground and its treasures stolen. According to the distraught priest, the raiding Goblins had carried off a prized artefact, a hammer that Sigmar himself had wielded. 

After following Kaia for several hours, we reached a wooded valley. Our approach afforded us a good view of the surroundings, and we could see several huts dotted around a larger one, the whole settlement surrounded by a rudimentary palisade. We wondered what sort of strength we were approaching and Professor von Gronighof advised caution. I admit that I shared his reticence. There were only the five of us, and this could have been an entire tribe of Goblins, or perhaps even a gathering of several tribes dedicated to raiding, or even preparing for a greater Waaagh! 

Professor Pfaff was immediately animated and insisted we pursue the Goblins and bring back the holy hammer whatever the cost. Von Gronighof was of course keen to continue his search for the sword. I, as an academic and historian, cannot help but wonder at the plethora of relics, talismans, and amulets that have survived through the twenty-five centuries since the time of Sigmar. And though I do not cast doubt on the provenance of any individual piece, I do doubt that of every piece, if only by the law of averages. 

Professor Pfaff was adamant, however, urging us to rescue the hammer as if we were to rescue Sigmar himself. And so we waited until nightfall. I am not sure, myself, of the wisdom of such a tactic. It has been observed on a number of occasions within the academic community that Goblins are comfortable in dim light and even darkness. If anything, it would give the Humans in our party, myself, Pfaff, and von Gronighof, a disadvantage. 

Kaia disappeared for an hour or so, to reconnoitre the settlement, and returned with news of a gap in the palisade from where we could reach the large central hut. We managed to squeeze between two of the planks that made up the rather rickety wall of that building and crawl into a corner of the hall. And what I saw there confounded me and has continued to do so as I have ruminated upon it ever since. 

For in the room, upon the ground in neat rows sat about two dozen Goblins. They were quiet and still, and their attention was fixed upon a single Goblin standing before them, shouting at them in their guttural tongue. Although admittedly there was some fidgeting at the back, and some seemed to be struggling to be so still and seemingly attentive. And this lead Goblin was dressed in rags, I thought, but when I had studied the scene and my eyes became accustomed to the light, I realised that these rags were the remnants of a religious robe, still bearing some of the ornamental stitching and symbols of the divine founder of our Empire. I wondered what foul fate had befallen the poor priest who had previously worn those tattered and defiled vestments. 

Behind the robed Goblin there was a lump of stone similar to the altars in many a temple across the Empire. And upon the stone sat the hammer that we had come to rescue. The robed Goblin addressed the hammer and lifted it above his head, showing it to the assembled Goblins. They let out a murmur of appreciation. This was not the sort of Goblin ritual I have seen attributed to them by those who have made a study of their barbarous culture, of course. This was, I gleaned, as close as they could make it, to a Sigmarite sermon. 

Pfaff made a similar deduction. He was livid. These creatures were performing some sort of blasphemous parody of our holy devotions. I could see him giving Sovrissniz the look that said, ‘Charge!’ I whispered for him to calm down, imploring him to wait for the right moment when we would have the advantage. Thankfully he controlled his rage. 

We waited until the middle of the night when most of the Goblins were sleeping and attempted to retrieve the holy hammer. Unfortunately, von Gronighof tripped over a sleeping Goblin, and we had to make a fighting retreat, with Kaia and Sovrissniz defending our rear. 

I think that was the only time Sovrissniz had enjoyed herself since we had tied the Goblin to the tree. But I am proud to say, that thanks to our efforts, the hammer now hangs in the temple once more. 

I was advised by the senior masters of the university not to publish this account. I only include it now in the knowledge that it will go no further than this correspondence. I have confidence in your discretion. What to make of it, I am flummoxed. Theories abound. Perhaps it is simply explained in the well-known phrase, ‘Goblin see. Goblin do.’ 

I am not sure what the Goblin deities might make of this, perhaps they encourage such eclecticism and assimilationism. Perhaps, as Pfaff suggests, they don’t exist. But I think the episode illustrates that the Goblins can learn. They are attentive and inquisitive. Some Human states might even learn from that example, though I will not name one, because I do not wish to discuss Bretonnia at this time. 

This sort of behaviour would explain the activity of the Broken Nose tribe. I have not encountered them myself but they are a good focus of scholarly debate, famous for their scavenged artillery. Do they understand the science behind their engines or even the practical applications behind the use of artillery? Did they observe the Dwarfs using their war machines and ape their actions, or did they, when faced with engines, equipment, ammunition, and a desired result, deduce the function through their own intellect? 

I have even read the thesis of a wizard of Ostland who has captured a Goblin that was scavenging about her tower. She painstakingly, over many years, taught the Goblin, whom she named Chatai, to read and write and then to even create complete written works of its own. She published a paper on her work, ‘Observations on food motivation and pain application on Goblin pre-training,’ which I have read, but could not honestly pretend to wholly understand. 

## **Tactics**
If the Broken Nose attack an army or settlement, they use their war machines and archers to soften up the target before charging in with mobs of infantry to mop up what’s left. If they’re accompanied by Datza’s wolf riders or the Trolls, they’ll send them ahead. 

Small patrols of Broken Nose Goblins attack opportunistically, peppering the enemy with arrow fire until they feel brave enough or impatient enough to charge in. No Goblin wants a fair fight, so they’ll employ any dirty trick or cunning ruse to make their victory as painless as possible. 

If the Broken Nose are attacked, they go into a frenzy of activity, trying to bring the war machines to bear. In practice, they can usually only ready a spear chukka to fire before becoming embroiled in melee. 

## **At Ease**
The Broken Nose tribe moves every few years, driven by a need for conquest and fear of the  harder Orc tribes who’d like to conquer them in turn. They live in crude tents amongst the crags and caves of hills and mountains. Boggrub and his mob always take the highest point in the camp and make sure the war-machines are dragged close so they can keep an eye on them. 

During the day, Broken Nose Goblins laze around until they’re kicked into doing something useful. They scout the area for threats and potential targets, hunt and forage for food, or deal with other greenskins nearby. Countless lesser tribes treat the Broken Nose with a modicum of respect, thanks to their reputation… or more precisely the reputation of their war machines. 

Some Goblins wander the mountain passes looking for fights — with Tilean patrols, Dwarfs or other greenskins. If the tribe grow bored, they fight amongst themselves and eat the Snotlings. It’s time to move — the Broken Nose load their belongings onto crude carts and the backs of the weaker Goblins then find a new place to live. 

## **Boggrub’s Gonna Kill Us! Easy Encounter**
Stink Dogjabber is notorious for his schemes and persuasive words. He talked Gutbug into lending him a spear chukka to hunt mountain goats, so the tribe could throw a feast to celebrate chasing off the Neck Snapper Orcs. They dragged the war engine up the hills, shot one goat and then watched its corpse plummet into a ravine, a waste of good meat. Worse still, on the way back, a wheel broke and now the spear chukka won’t move. 

The Characters can encounter this scene when passing through the mountains. Several Goblins surround a bolt thrower with a broken wheel. They’re arguing in the greenskin tongue, pointing at one another — deep in the blame game. Stink wears an over-sized helmet and ragged mail. It’s a tense moment which may erupt in violence, with some accusing Stink of stealing and all of them terrified of what will happen if news of this gets back to Boggrub. 

When the Goblins see the Characters, they’re reluctant to abandon the spear chukka. They surround the war engine, ready to fight with their spears while a few take up their short bows and start shooting. The Characters can attack or even help fix the wheel. If they charge, the Goblins try to load and fire the spear chukka at them. 

If the Characters overcome the Goblins, Stink tries to make sure he survives. He rats out of the rest of the tribe in broken Reikspiel, telling the Characters where they can be found, their weak points, and where they keep their prized war engines. 

- Stink (Elite) gesticulating madly and waving his spear. 

- Four Goblins (Soldiers) standing behind Stink trying to look menacing. 

- Three Goblins (Skirmishers) with bows, also arguing. 

- Spear chukka with two crew (Skirmishers with Ranged (Crossbow) +10), arms folded, remonstrating with Stink). 

## **Stunty on the Loose Medium Encounter**
Kargun Grimbarden finally plucked up the courage to escape his captors and make for civilisation. Years of humiliation and shame have made him desperate enough to take his chances in the mountains. When Boggrub discovered Kargun’s escape, he despatched Gutbug to track him down, accompanied by Rutbagger, Pusboil and their swiftest Goblins. 

This encounter begins when the Characters find Kargun stumbling through the hills or mountains, exhausted, malnourished, and panicked. He begs them for help in a cracked voice, tears streaming down his hairless face. 1d10 Rounds later, the Goblins barrel around a bend in the mountain path and an observant archer spots the Characters. If they act swiftly, they can escape to safety. Fortunately for them, there is a Dwarf patrol a mile further down the path. 

The Goblins want to take Kargun back alive. Their numbers mean they think they can take the Characters, especially with Rutbagger’s spells on their side. They approach slowly, to give four archers and two spears time to sneak behind the party to prevent their escape. If the Goblins are defeated or the party gets away, a few Goblins run back to Boggrub and tell him Gutbug messed up. 

Until Kargun is safe and miles from the Broken Nose tribe, he won’t reveal his story or what he’s done. If the Characters don’t help him, he’ll warn them the local Goblins have war machines and have tortured him for many years. He won’t admit his role in keeping the war engines in working order. 

## **I Want Dat Gun! Hard Encounter**
The Broken Nose tribe have come down from the hills to assault the village of Michelfurt in Wissenland, confident their war engines and numbers can overwhelm the measly regiment posted in Schloss Michel, which sits within the village. Boggrub knows the tribe shall enjoy despoiling a Human village, but he has another reason for attacking — his scouts told him an Imperial Engineer is holed up in the fort with a Volley Gun. This would be a spectacular addition to the tribe’s artillery. 

This encounter could happen if the Party are staying in Michelfurt or on the road, where they hear tell of Goblins approaching a nearby village. It’s easy to relocate this encounter to any location which borders the mountains in the southern Empire, Tilea, or the Border Princes. Boggrub orders an assault on the village at dusk, using tried-and-tested tactics which served him well on many occasions. The tribe uses Skull Crusher to pound the village, palisade, and Schloss with rocks, before firing on the gate with all the war engines. When they think the locals are sufficiently demoralised, Pusboil’s Guard, and Stink’s Dogjabbers charge through the gate and breached palisade to attack the villagers and Schloss Michel. 

The village will fall if the men-at-arms aren’t helped by the Characters. The Schloss’s commander, August von Clausewitz, did not see the attack coming and struggles to make decisions under pressure. The Imperial Engineer, Agathe Eichalt, has only enough powder to fire one volley from her artillery piece, which is hastily armed in the gatehouse of the fort. 

   - Boggrub and his mob, including Rutbagger.

- Nine Archers (Skirmishers) with bows. 

- A Stone Troll and three Snotlings, who have no idea what’s going on. They just tagged along because it looked like fun.

## **Boggrub Legbiter – Goblin Warlord**
Boggrub is warchief of the Broken Nose tribe. He keeps his position because he’s a little smarter and sneakier than the rest of the Goblins under his command, who harbour a superstitious belief that he’s somehow blessed by Mork. He’s burlier than the other Goblins, with muscular arms, and a particularly ugly, toothy grimace under his broken nose. Boggrub wears a pointed metal helmet, looted chainmail, and wields a very sharp Dwarfen sword. 

Boggrub is restless, devious, and careful to surround himself with henchmen less intelligent and ambitious than himself. 32 years ago, Boggrub lead a Waaagh! through the eastern mountains, which forged their reputation amongst greenskins. Boggrub knows a Goblin warlord’s position is tenuous, as Orcs and treacherous underlings are always looking to depose him. For Boggrub, the tribe’s stolen war machines are more than just weapons — they’re the reason he stays on top of the heap. 

Very few Goblins live as long as Boggrub, and there are whispers amongst the tribe suggesting this isn’t the original Boggrub. Dwarfen lorekeepers believe today’s Broken Nose is led by the third Goblin of that name. Nobody knows except Boggrub himself — and he’s saying nothing.

## **Ratlicker – Goblin Soldier**
Ratlicker is typical of the grubby, mendacious Goblins who populate the Broken Nose tribe. He was initiated by Boggrub just three years ago and since his nose healed, he’s become a moderately-dependable second rank Goblin in Stink’s Dogjabbers. 

Ratlicker is a shade more disciplined than some of his fellows, but only because he has a pointier spear, which instills him with a certain pride. Otherwise, Ratlicker does not stand out from the rest of the mob. He wears a tatty and greasy chainmail shirt and stands with a distinct stoop. Ratlicker wants the Broken Nose to conquer more Dwarf outposts because he believes he should have a shield and nicking one from a dead stunty is better than making or trading for one.  During the day, Ratlicker wastes time bickering with the other Goblins in his mob. His favourite hobby is kicking Snotlings at the Trolls to watch them get eaten.

## **Kargun Grimbarden**
When Boggrub attacked the outpost near Karak Azgal, everything changed for Kargun Grimbarden. Almost every Dwarf in the tunnels was slaughtered by grinning, vicious Goblins who pounded the fortifications with a stolen runic stone thrower. Kargun was just a beardling, barely more than 25 years old, when Boggrub hauled him from amongst the dead and demanded he show the grobi how to use a cannon. To his shame, he did what they asked — and sealed his doom. 

Since that fateful day 32 years ago, Kargun has been a captive of the Broken Nose tribe, forced to maintain their war engines. His life is an unending torment of unconquerable anguish. He has never managed to escape and, thanks to him, many Dwarfs have died at the hand of Boggrub’s machineries of destruction. He almost fears freedom, as how would he show his (beardless) face to another Dwarf, knowing what he’s done? 

Kargun is a broken Dwarf. The Goblins have shaved his beard, and broken his nose. He is missing several toes as Gutbug ate them to encourage Kargun to clean out Lead Belcher’s barrels faster.

## **Orc and Goblin War Machines**
Greenskins use war engines of various kinds — with the exception of Savage Orcs who disdain anything that reeks of ‘progress’ and Forest Goblins who find eight-legged beasts work better in the dense woods where they live. 

The challenge for greenskins is they don’t like maintaining complex equipment — it’s complicated and boring. Most war engines are maintained by Goblins, who are more intelligent and have better fine motor skills than Orcs. Orcs on the march want to destroy things, not chop up countless bits of wood for some addle-brained siege engineer. The bone-idle laxity of Goblins ensures greenskin war engines fall apart and kill their crew reasonably often. 

When greenskins harness the power of their war engines, they become a serious threat, able to take on heavilyarmoured opponents and attack fortified settlements. The Broken Nose Goblins are a good example of a tribe whose conquests are only impressive thanks to their unique machineries of destruction. In battle, Goblin crews scurry about fetching ammunition, loading the machines, and firing. The crew is sometimes overseen by an Orc ‘bully’, an artillerist who stands around encouraging the Goblins to work faster with his fists or a handy club. 

Greenskin war engines vary in design, but there are recurring patterns — mainly copied from other species by an enterprising Goblin in the past and mimicked ever since. Orc and Goblin Warlords demand huge siege engines when their armies attack settlements. Their mobs swiftly hack down trees to hammer together ramshackle siege towers, battering rams, and huge rock lobbers. They may resemble giant effigies of Mork and Gork, with leering wooden heads which disgorge Orcs and Goblins from their mouths onto the enemy ramparts. 

## **Spear Chukkas**
These are ballistae, influenced many thousands of years ago by greenskins copying Dwarfen equivalents. No greenskin can resist the simple pleasures of watching an enemy speared on a massive bolt. Essentially giant crossbows, spear chukkas are fairly easy to build and repair, although they’re still less reliable than ballistae built by other species. They are a common sight on the battlefield, on fortifications, and on board the largest of their boats. Hobgoblins craft better, wheeled spear chukkas, suited to their nomadic lifestyle. 

## **Rock Lobbers**
Any kind of greenskin catapult is called a rock lobber, regardless of how it works — if it can lob a big rock at the enemy, it’s a rock lobber. There are many different designs… trebuchets, onagers, mangonels… greenskins can’t pronounce these names, but they’ll cheerfully build one if they can. 

Projectiles aren’t limited to rocks. Heavy captives work very well, especially a fat little Dwarf in plate armour or a few Gobbos trussed together. Snotlings can be fired from rock lobbers to deliver messages to enemies. Assuming they survive the landing, they recite what they have been told by rote. 

## **Doom Divers**
This is a small catapult designed to fire a Goblin high into the air. This brave lunatic wears hand-stitched leather wings which they use to direct their ascent and descent, with devastating consequences for whoever they hit on landing. A surprising number of Doom Diver Goblins survive, eager to take another flight high above the earth. 

## Playing Both Sides
The Red Tusk Orcs of the Middle Mountains are gearing up for another incursion into Middenland, so they need weapons. Herr Flugbeg of Frote is a man without morals who deals in arms, buying the produce of smiths in southern Nordland and selling it in bulk to anyone who’s buying — preferably both sides in a fight, for maximum profit. He’ll pay handsomely for someone to escort his cargo from Frote to Oberholzbeck, where his greenskin buyers await and can dispose of anyone who can tell of Flugbeg’s crimes. 

## Git Da Plans
Notlob is an Orc with an unusual appetite for invention. His renowned battery of spear chukkas have been the ruin of many an army. He’s looking to improve on his creations by finding the formula for Helstorm rockets, an explosive weapon employed by the Imperial Engineer’s Guild, He knows cunning is a better ploy than brute force, so he wants to lure an Engineer into the Black Mountains somehow… probably using Human dupes as intermediaries.

## **New Weapon Flaw Crewed**
A weapon with the _Crewed_ Flaw is so large, heavy, and complex that it benefits from being managed by a team rather than a single operator. This team all need to possess the relevant _Ranged_ Skill to crew the weapon. However, they may nominate one of their number to make the relevant Ranged Test to see how well the weapon performs when it is triggered. 

Most weapons have a crew of 2, 3, or 4. Larger crews are often assembled, but extraneous crew members do not impact the efficiency of the weapon itself, though they may help move it or make up for casualties among the crew. 

Penalties from reduced crew are cumulative, so a _Crewed 4_ weapon with a single crewman will suffer from double reload time, the _Imprecise_ Flaw, and the _Shoddy_ Flaw. 

If a weapon gains a Flaw that it already possesses, impose a further penalty of –10 to any Ranged Tests made to shoot the weapon. 

When reloading a weapon with the _Crewed_ Flaw, one of the crew may assist with any Tests made to determine how long the reloading process takes. 

If a weapon with the _Crewed_ Flaw suffers a misfire, all members of the crew are affected. 

If a weapon requiring a crew is not fully crewed, it is impaired as explained in the table below.

## Notes on Doom Divers
Doom Divers do not use ammunition like normal catapults. Instead they shoot Goblins. They have no _Crewed_ flaw, as the Goblin himself aims and operates the small catapult. As long as there are willing Goblins equipped with leather batwings, the Doom Diver may continue shooting. 

## Goblin Artillery Crew
Goblin artillery crew use the Basic Common Goblin profile with the addition of the _Ranged (Crossbow)_ +10 or _Ranged (Catapult)_ +10 Skills.
